stories.title: Congress holds padayatra demanding removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar

article_sentences: Congress party leaders and workers on Tuesday took out a padayatra in Yadgir, demanding the immediate removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, accusing the Election Commission of India (ECI) of functioning under political pressure from the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) at the Centre.

Led by Yadgir MLA Channareddy Patil Tunnur, a large number of supporters marched from Mailapur Base through key thoroughfares before culminating in a public rally at Gandhi Chowk in the old town area.
Addressing the demonstration, Mr. Tunnur alleged that the Union government had been abusing power and manipulating constitutional bodies, including the ECI, to compromise the integrity of elections.
He claimed that recent measures taken under the leadership of Mr. Kumar had disproportionately affected the voting rights of Dalits, Backward Classes, minorities, and economically weaker sections.

”The Chief Election Commissioner, who is expected to act independently and uphold constitutional norms, has surrendered to the political interests of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah to benefit the BJP,” Mr. Tunnur said, adding that Mr. Kumar must be sacked immediately to ensure free and fair elections in the future.

Speaking at the gathering, District Congress Committee (DCC) president Basareddy Anapur and party leaders Sharanappa Manegar, Krishna Chepetla, and Samson Malikeri condemned the Union government for undermining democratic institutions.
They said that the protest was part of a broader nationwide agitation launched by the Congress party, which would continue until the Chief Election Commissioner is removed from the office.
Local leaders, including Siddalingareddy Ullesugur, Saibanna Borbanda, Mallikarjun Ete, Raghavendra Manasagal, and Laxman Rathod, were present.

stories.headline: Did SIR deletions change Tamil Nadu assembly election’s outcome?
stories.title: Did SIR deletions change Tamil Nadu assembly election’s outcome?
stories.summary: While a businessline analysis reveals a striking geographical overlap between high voter removals and TVK victories, experts urge caution against reading it as a conspiracy
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) have stirred protests not just at the national but at the State level too.
In Tamil Nadu, DMK president and former Chief Minister MK Stalin has recently said that the deletion of several lakh voters was one of the reasons for his party’s loss.
The social media is abuzz about how TVK victory may have been aided by these deletions.
A businessline analysis of the granular data on SIR deletions and the outcome of the TN assembly elections in 2026, throws us some interesting trends.
TVK has struggled to win in constituencies where the SIR deletions were lower but has recorded more wins in constituencies where the deletions were higher.
Political analysts and experts however warn that not much should be read into these numbers.
We compared the net reduction in voter count in each constituency as per the April 2026 electoral roll with pre-SIR numbers.
Of the total 234 constituencies, 19 constituencies had lower deletions, of up to 10,000 voters.
In these, the TVK won 2 seats, the DMK 7, the AIADMK 6 and others 4.
Eighty constituencies had deletions between 10,000 to 20,000 voters.
The TVK won 22 of these constituencies, the DMK 20, the AIADMK 24 and others 14.
Sixty-six constituencies had deletions between 20,000 to 30,000.

stories.headline: Indian opposition MPs detained in protest against election chief
stories.title: Indian opposition MPs detained in protest against election chief
stories.summary: Opposition leaders have alleged that CEC Gyanesh Kumar manipulated voter rolls to favour Prime Minister Narendra Modi's party during elections.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Police in Delhi detained several opposition lawmakers as they tried to march demanding the chief election commissioner resign over a controversial voter roll revision.
Main opposition leader Rahul Gandhi, his sister Priyanka and other MPs were forced into a police bus.
Released shortly after, they resumed their march and began a sit-in near Election Commission headquarters.
It is the latest escalation in a growing row over a nationwide revision of voter rolls.

Opposition parties accuse Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of overseeing a process that could benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), an allegation both the BJP and Election Commission have rejected.
"Some of the MPs tried to take some other roads to the Election Commission building.

We have officers stationed at multiple points, from where the protesters were picked up in buses and taken to different police stations," Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police Manjeet Sheoran told the BBC.
The police did not disclose how many lawmakers had been detained.
The opposition said 237 MPs from a range of parties participated in the march.

Tuesday's protest came just four days after the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a Gen Z-backed online satirical movement, organised demonstrations in Mumbai and Delhi, also demanding the CEC's resignation.
The group has described those demonstrations as the beginning of a nationwide campaign and has called for another round of protests on 10 October.
At the centre of the controversy is the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

stories.headline: Cabinet approves Rs 10,000 crore SME Growth Fund to create future champions
stories.title: Cabinet approves Rs 10,000 crore SME Growth Fund to create future champions
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 06: The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, on Monday approved the government’s commitment of Rs 10,000 crore towards establishing the SME Growth Fund (SGF) to provide growth capital to small and medium enterprises and help create Indian companies capable of competing globally. The initiative, announced as part of the Union Budget 2026-27, seeks to address the structural gap in growth-stage equity financing available to SMEs, particularly those looking to scale operations, adopt advanced technologies, expand internationally and integrate into global value chains. Under the scheme, the government will provide an aggregate commitment of Rs 10,000 crore to an Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) established under the SGF framework. The fund will focus primarily on small and medium manufacturing enterprises, while also considering SMEs operating in industrial clusters in Tier-II and Tier-III cities. The government said the fund is designed to provide patient, long-term equity capital to high-potential SMEs with demonstrated business viability and scalability. The initiative is expected to help enterprises expand capacity, improve productivity, adopt new technologies, enter international markets and undertake strategic investments, thereby strengthening their competitiveness and export potential. The government said the SGF would complement existing measures aimed at strengthening the SME ecosystem, including credit support, digitalisation, ease of doing business reforms, public procurement measures, startup promotion and production-linked incentive programmes. The initiative is also expected to support balanced regional industrial development, strengthen local supply chains and generate quality employment, particularly through investments in industrial clusters in Tier-II and Tier-III cities. The government said the fund would help foster a new generation of competitive Indian enterprises and contribute to the vision of Viksit Bharat @ 2047.

stories.title: Omar Abdullah welcomes SC scrutiny of voter deletions, rules out UCC in J&K
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 06: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Tuesday welcomed the Supreme Court’s intervention in the issue of voter deletions, said the INDIA bloc’s campaign against the Election Commission would continue and ruled out implementing the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) in the Union Territory. Speaking to reporters, Abdullah said the INDIA bloc had finalised a calendar of programmes during a recent meeting in Delhi, with the campaign beginning with a march by its Members of Parliament to the Election Commission. “Today’s programme was a march to the Election Commission, and this campaign will continue,” he said. Abdullah said the media had begun highlighting concerns over voter deletions, an issue he claimed had repeatedly been raised by the opposition. “It is a good thing that questions are now being raised in the Supreme Court as well,” he said, referring to the court seeking responses from the Election Commission and the Government of India on the deletion of names from electoral rolls and the basis for those deletions. “We will have to wait and see to what extent the matter can be rectified through the courts,” he added. ‘ We will not implement UCC here’ On the Uniform Civil Code, Abdullah categorically ruled out its implementation in Jammu and Kashmir and questioned the BJP’s approach of pursuing the measure through individual states. “We will not implement the Uniform Civil Code here,” he said, adding that several other state governments had also opposed its implementation. Abdullah argued that a law intended to be uniform should be debated and considered at the national level rather than introduced separately by individual states. “If they have the courage, let them bring a law in Parliament and debate it there. Let us see whether it gets passed,” he said. Claiming that the BJP did not have the numbers to secure the passage of such legislation in Parliament, Abdullah alleged that the party was pursuing the measure incrementally through states where it was in power. “That is why the BJP is implementing it gradually, state by state, which is wrong,” he said. “If we look at democracy in its true sense, this issue should be debated at the Centre and not separately in different states,” he added. He said the refugees had been allowed to stay until conditions in their country improved. “When they were driven out of their own country, we gave them shelter and some space to stay here until conditions in their country improved,” Abdullah said. “Taking action against them suddenly now seems strange to me,” he added. The chief minister, however, said the matter was beyond the control of his government, as the action was being taken by the Government of India with police assistance. “The police are not under our control either. It would be better to put these questions to those who exercise command over the police,” he said. He said the Cabinet had decided to allot land to BSNL in areas without mobile signals to facilitate the installation of mobile towers. Explaining the decision on underground ducts, Abdullah said roads were frequently dug up by different departments to lay water pipelines, electricity infrastructure and telecommunications cables. “One department after another keeps digging up the roads,” he said. He said installing ducts during road construction would allow departments to use the same infrastructure instead of repeatedly excavating roads. “That was the purpose of the decision. Now it needs to be implemented,” he said. After that, we will tell you what we have done and what we have not done,” he said. body: The swearing-in ceremony, which was live-streamed, was held at 3.30 p.m., marking a departure from the usual practice of administering the oath to newly appointed Supreme Court judges in the morning.
Newly appointed Supreme Court judges usually take the oath of office at 10.30 a.m., coinciding with the time when the top court assembles on working days to conduct hearings.
The three Chief Justices of the High Courts took the oath as judges of the apex court after the Centre cleared their elevation on the recommendation of the Supreme Court Collegium this week.

"The Supreme Court Collegium in its meeting held on 28th September, 2026 has recommended elevation of the following Chief Justices of the High Courts as Judges in the Supreme Court," the Collegium had said in a statement uploaded on the apex court's official website.
Acting swiftly on the Collegium's recommendation, the Centre on Monday approved the elevation of Justices Agarwal, Upadhyaya, and Singh.

In a post on X, Union Minister for Law and Justice Arjun Ram Meghwal announced that the President, after consultation with CJI Surya Kant, had appointed the three Chief Justices as judges of the apex court.
Justice Agarwal, born on April 30, 1966, was appointed as a judge of the Allahabad High Court on November 21, 2011.
She became the Chief Justice of the Gujarat High Court on July 23, 2023.
Justice Upadhyaya, born on June 16, 1965, was appointed as a puisne Judge of the Allahabad High Court on November 21, 2011 and became a permanent Judge on August 6, 2013.
He became the Senior Judge of the Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court on March 28, 2023.

He was appointed Chief Justice of the Bombay High Court and took the oath on July 29, 2023, before being transferred as Chief Justice of the Delhi High Court, where he took the oath on January 21, 2025.
Justice Singh, born on July 7, 1965, was appointed as an Additional Judge of the Jharkhand High Court on January 24, 2012 and was confirmed as a Permanent Judge on January 16, 2014.
He served as Acting Chief Justice of the Jharkhand High Court from December 20, 2022, to February 19, 2023.
He took the oath as Chief Justice of the Tripura High Court on April 17, 2023, and was subsequently transferred as Chief Justice of the Telangana High Court, where he took the oath on July 19, 2025.
The appointments will further strengthen the Supreme Court's judicial strength following the Centre's decision earlier this year to increase the sanctioned strength to 37, excluding the CJI.

stories.summary: The World Bank has raised its growth forecast for India for the current fiscal year to 7.1 percent, 0.5 percentage points higher than it earlier expected, saying strong industrial and services momentum, backed by a series of reforms, will keep the economy ahead of most peers despite costlier energy. However, the number is a moderation from the 7.8 percent recorded in FY26, which itself beat the Bank’s April estimate of 7.6 percent. Growth is seen edging up to 7.2 percent in FY28.In its October edition of the South Asia Economic Update, the World Bank noted: “The country’s growth potential remains strong, supported by a series of major reforms, such as labour code consolidation, GST reforms, tariff rationalisation, the Insolvency Act, and infrastructure investments for both the real and digital economy.”Also Read: N Chandrasekaran: Energy, Manufacturing Jobs Key to Viksit Bharat 2047Investment has gained momentum over the past three quarters, growing more than 10 percent in April-June, and strong credit growth is expected to keep supporting it. “Services and industry expanded at a healthy pace, particularly manufacturing, construction, and power, offsetting some weakness in energy-intensive sectors such as chemicals, and weaker agricultural growth following the delayed monsoon,” the report noted.India’s external position also looks comfortable. The current account deficit was held at 0.6 percent of GDP in FY26, though it widened in April-June as higher oil imports swelled the goods trade deficit, partly offset by a strong services surplus. The rupee fell more than 10 percent between March 2025 and June 2026 but has stabilised as oil prices eased and capital flows strengthened, helped by deposits raised through the FCNR bank facility. Foreign exchange reserves recovered to $752 billion by end-August, covering nearly 11 months of merchandise imports. Remittances to India have grown by more than 30 percent so far this year, and asset quality in banks remains strong.However, the downside risks to the Indian economy also remain. India has just endured its fourth-driest June-August period since 1960—this rain deficit could further exert “upward pressure” on food prices. On the two earlier occasions when monsoon rainfall ran about 20 percent below normal, agricultural output ended up 4-5 percent below trend. Despite these risks, however, the Bank expects strength elsewhere in the economy to offset farm weakness.Also Read: Factory GVA rises 9.6 percent to Rs26.9 lakh crore in FY25: ASIConsumer confidence, though elevated, slid to a three-year low in July. The report also noted that India’s policy response to the energy shock has combined softer conservation steps, such as remote work with medium-term efforts to promote electric vehicles and fuel switching.However, the report’s special focus on artificial intelligence offers a sobering note. About 23.4 percent of formal Indian firms use some form of AI, against 42.7 percent in the United States, and the gap widens with sophistication. India scores 0.27 on the Bank’s AI adoption index versus 0.85 for the US. Only 3.5 percent of Indian firms have paid for AI, compared with 23.1 percent of American firms, with cost the most cited barrier. Still, ICT already accounts for over 22 percent of India’s exports, and grid reliability, led by India, now exceeds the average for emerging markets.For the wider South Asian region, the Bank sees growth of 6.9 percent in 2026 and 6.7 percent in 2027, keeping South Asia the fastest-growing emerging-market region.

article_sentences: The Bombay High Court on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) adjourned the hearing on a writ petition filed by a family in Goa against the deletion of their names from the electoral roll, as the Election Commission of India (ECI) contended that the Supreme Court was dealing with petitions challenging the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).
“The orders the Supreme Court may pass can have a bearing on the matter before the High Court,” said advocate Gaurish Agni, representing the ECI.
Justices Valmiki Menezes and Amit Jamsandekar of the High Court's Goa Bench then postponed the hearing to next Tuesday (October 13, 2026).
Advocate Agni told reporters that the ECI placed before the High Court "some orders of the Hon'ble Supreme Court and orders passed by three or four other High Courts."

"The Supreme Court has issued directions in some SIR petitions pending before it that wherever there is a challenge to the SIR and deletion of names, if a petition is presented before a High Court, ideally the hearing should be deferred," he said.
“Similar orders have also been passed by the Sikkim, Uttarakhand and Kerala High Courts,” the lawyer said.

"Therefore, my argument before the court today was that since the Hon'ble Supreme Court is seized of the SIR issue, including the issue of deletion of voters from the draft roll, the orders that may be passed by the Supreme Court could have some bearing on this matter," he said.
The petition before the Goa Bench of the High Court also involves the deletion of names from the draft roll and consequential rejection of Form 8, Advocate Agni added.

“The High Court judges were of the view that the Supreme Court's orders may not have a direct bearing on this matter, but the ECI requested that the hearing be adjourned for a week as the Supreme Court was likely to hear the petitions before it on October 8,” he said.
“In the case before the High Court, the SIR, guidelines or the forms have not been challenged, but "what is under challenge is the rejection of Form 8," the ECI lawyer said.
"Our argument is that Form 8 cannot be looked at in isolation," he said, adding that it happens when enumeration form is not collected.
The ECI's argument is that Form 8 has to be read along with the process that takes place prior to its submission, advocate Agni added.

stories.headline: Cabinet approves proposal to set up Integrated Transport and Logistics Authority
stories.title: Cabinet approves proposal to set up Integrated Transport and Logistics Authority
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 6: The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, today approved the setting up of a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV), namely, Integrated Transport & Logistics Authority (ITLA) to strengthen research, planning, appraisal, monitoring and impact assessment within the broad domains of Transportation and Logistics. The approval seeks to address the long-standing challenges arising from fragmented planning and implementation across multiple transport-related Ministries and agencies. By fostering greater coordination and multi-modal integration, ITLA is expected to enhance the efficiency, sustainability and effectiveness of transport infrastructure development in India. ITLA will have following key roles and responsibilities: National Apex Institution: ITLA will function as the apex body for integrated transport and logistics planning, research, project appraisal and monitoring, policy support and data analytics. Long-Term National Transport Master Plan: ITLA will prepare a comprehensive National Transport Master Plan with a planning horizon of ten years or more, covering roads, railways, ports and shipping, civil aviation, inland waterways, coastal shipping, urban mobility and logistics. Integrated Planning Framework: ITLA will evaluate short-term sectoral plans (5 years or so) and annual plans of transport Ministries to ensure consistency and alignment with the National Transport Master Plan and promote multi-modal infrastructure development. Technical Appraisal of Major Projects: ITLA will undertake technical appraisal of infrastructure projects of Government of India, costing Rs.500 crore or more. Financial appraisal will continue to be carried out through the existing financial appraisal mechanisms. Monitoring and Impact Assessment: ITLA will monitor implementation of transport & infrastructure projects above Rs.500 crore and provide a coordinated mechanism for issue resolution and will undertake post-implementation impact assessment of these projects. National Transport Data Repository (NTDR): ITLA will build a unified transport data repository by obtaining relevant transport and logistics datasets from multiple sources, including GSTN e-way bill, FASTag, Vahan, GPS-based systems, urban traffic management systems and other relevant databases and carry out data analytics (e.g. Freight Flow/O-D analytics) for planning, monitoring and impact assessment. Advise and assist for review and updation of National Logistics Policy (2022) Capacity building, training, and skilling in the logistics sector. Promote Research & Innovations in transport and logistics sectors. Establishment of the ITLA will play a pivotal role in realizing India’s Vision 2047 by strengthening multimodal connectivity, improving infrastructure efficiency, reducing logistics costs, and enhancing India’s global logistics competitiveness. The ITLA will build institutional capacity for research, planning, big data integration, project monitoring, and evaluation, while supporting capacity building and adoption of international best practices.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday (05 October) has set aside the conviction of a government employee under Sections 7 and 13 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 (PC Act) who had already served his sentence, holding that the prosecution failed to prove demand and acceptance of illegal gratification.

A bench of Justice Ujjal Bhuyan and Justice Atul S Chandurkar held so while hearing an appeal filed by the government employee who had already served his sentence, and had pursued the appeal only to “get his name cleared.”
The appellant was an Assistant in the District Education Office and the complainant (PW 1) was appointed as an orderly in a Government High School but was not paid his salary.
It was alleged that the appellant demanded Rs 5,000 as bribe in 2010 for releasing the salary.
Thereafter, the complainant approached the Vigilance Bureau pursuant to which a trap was laid down leading to the arrest of the appellant and recovery of tainted money of Rs 5,000.

The Special Judge convicted the accused (appellant) under Sections 7 and 13(2) in 2021, sentencing him to rigorous imprisonment for four years and a fine of Rs 10,000 for each offence, with concurrent sentence.
Thereafter, he appealed before the Jharkhand High Court which dismissed his plea in 2022.
Aggrieved by the High Court's dismissal, the accused (appellant) approached the Supreme Court.
Before the Supreme Court, the appellant apprised the bench that he had undergone the sentence and paid the fine, but wished to pursue the matter to get his name cleared.
He argued that demand and acceptance of illegal gratification were not proved beyond reasonable doubt and that the prosecution relied entirely on the uncorroborated testimony of the complainant.
It was pointed out that the alleged transaction took place inside the appellant's residence, in the absence of the trap team and without any shadow or independent witness.

It was argued that the recovery of tainted money could not prove demand and acceptance, and that the phenolphthalein test (which confirmed that the money recovered was tainted) was conducted belatedly.

stories.headline: Cabinet hails PM Modi's 25 years of uninterrupted leadership as head of govt
stories.title: Cabinet hails PM Modi's 25 years of uninterrupted leadership as head of govt
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 6: The Union Cabinet on Tuesday hailed PM Narendra Modi's 25 years of uninterrupted leadership as the head of government, first as the Gujarat CM and then as the prime minister, saying his "extraordinary journey" was guided by the principle of "Nation First and Citizen First". In a resolution, the cabinet also said that three overwhelming mandates in Gujarat and support in three successive Lok Sabha elections reflect the "enduring trust" that the public has reposed in Prime Minister Modi. Briefing reporters on the resolution adopted at the cabinet meeting, Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said the cabinet passed the resolution congratulating the prime minister on completing 25 years of continuous leadership as head of government. "Far more than a customary tribute, it celebrates the extraordinary journey of PM Modi guided by the principle of 'Nation First and Citizen First'," he said. Vaishnaw said ten salient features capture the unbroken thread connecting his leadership in Gujarat with his leadership later as the country's PM. Firstly, the resolution lauded how PM Modi carried Gujarat's successful initiatives to the national stage. It cited the example of SWAGAT through which he personally heard citizens' grievances. The grievance tracking portal, which received the United Nations Public Service Award in 2010, later inspired PRAGATI, bringing governments together to review stalled projects, resolve obstacles and accelerate completion. Jyotigram scheme's separate agricultural electricity feeders similarly extended Gujarat's experience across India, Vaishnaw said. Secondly, the resolution underscored that PM Modi's sensitivity towards poverty grew from watching his mother struggle with everyday hardships and encountering deprivation during his travels. The minister said the resolution connects these experiences with programmes delivering homes, water, banking and healthcare. "Nearly 60 crore Jan Dhan accounts, over 4 crore homes and 25 crore people moving out of poverty show how personal understanding became public action, bringing families dignity," read a statement listing the highlights of the resolution. The resolution also said PM Modi's determination to help people across society shape their futures is exemplified in the approximately 3.5 crore 'Lakhpati Didis', and the women's reservation provided in the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam. Startups, skills and education reform under his government have expanded youth opportunities, it said. PM-KISAN transfers exceeded Rs 4 lakh crore, while PM-JANMAN brought focused support to particularly vulnerable tribal communities, extending development to those historically left behind, Vaishnaw said. The resolution also gives particular emphasis to PM Modi's willingness to pursue reform despite political risks. GST, welfare delivery reforms and the replacement of colonial laws demonstrate his determination to address longstanding challenges, it said. The minister said Modi's appeals on cleanliness, digital payments and local products drew citizens into change. "Reform emerges as a sustained commitment of his leadership, strengthened by conviction, public participation and national purpose," it said. The resolution noted the foundations of a self-reliant India built under PM Modi's leadership. Public capital expenditure rose from Rs 2 lakh crore to over Rs 12 lakh crore, alongside highway expansion and railway electrification, it said. Vaishnaw said electronics production increased from around Rs 2 lakh crore to more than Rs 13 lakh crore and defence production and semiconductor manufacturing further reflect his determination to strengthen India's ability to meet its needs. The resolution also highlighted that PM Modi's faith in technology emerges through achievements in everyday services and scientific frontiers. The minister said Jan Dhan, Aadhaar and mobile connectivity improved welfare delivery, while UPI transformed payments. "Developing India's own COVID vaccines and landing Chandrayaan-3 near the Moon's south pole demonstrated PM Modi's vision of a scientifically capable, self-reliant, Atmanirbhar Bharat," it said. Private space participation and work in artificial intelligence, quantum technology and biotechnology carry forward the vision celebrated in the resolution: technology improving lives while expanding national possibilities, the minister said. The resolution also lauds PM Modi's "steadfast leadership through turbulent times", and his ability to "give India direction through global upheaval". Vaishnaw said during COVID-19, Modi united the country, backed domestic vaccine development and enabled rapid vaccination. During the West Asia crisis, timely decisions and energy security measures helped India withstand disruption and his leadership combined immediate responses with capabilities built over years, giving the country resilience and confidence in difficult times, he said. The resolution credits Modi's "decisive leadership" for securing peace and public trust. It said the 2016 Surgical Strikes, 2019 Balakot Air Strikes and 2025 Operation Sindoor illustrate the national security red lines established under PM Modi. The minister said the resolution places these alongside the removal of Article 370, One Rank One Pension and creation of the Chief of Defence Staff's post. Action against Maoist terrorism and peace efforts in the northeast shows his leadership to be combining national resolve with development, stability and public trust, it said. The resolution linked India's rising stature in the world with PM Modi's ability to build cooperation across divisions. Vaishnaw said consensus at G20 and BRICS, advocacy for the Global South and the African Union's G20 inclusion reflect his diplomatic leadership. While 'Vaccine Maitri' demonstrated how India's capabilities could serve others, honours from 36 countries underline the international regard for PM Modi and India's growing influence and contribution to shared solutions, he said. According to the resolution, the prime minister's vision unites development, cultural confidence and environmental responsibility. As Gujarat CM, Modi formed an independent department for climate change, and now as PM, he has overseen an expansion of renewable energy and international partnerships in the sector. The minister said yoga, millets, Kashi Vishwanath Dham and Ram Lalla's consecration have strengthened India's connection with its heritage. The resolution ends with a renewed commitment to his vision of collective effort towards a prosperous, self-reliant and developed India by 2047, he said.

stories.headline: IMD: Heavy rain over TN, Kerala, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh & Karnataka
stories.title: IMD: Heavy rain over TN, Kerala, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh & Karnataka
stories.summary: IMD expects to see evolving Bay of Bengal circulation to intensify as a low-pressure area, or even depression, by October 15, which is the normal date of onset for North-East monsoon
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The South-West monsoon showed little inclination to retreat on Tuesday, with its withdrawal line remaining unchanged from Monday even as heavy rain continued to sweep across the South Peninsula in what could be an increasingly wet run-up to North-East monsoon.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) expects conditions to become favourable for withdrawal of the monsoon from more parts of East and North-East India and adjoining areas of north Peninsular India during this week and into next.
But the transition could prove less orderly than usual, with the retreating monsoon and the advancing north-east monsoon potentially overlapping in time.
The stakes are rising because a potentially important weather system is likely taking shape over the Bay of Bengal.
Heavy to very heavy rain lashed parts of Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal from Monday to Tuesday, while heavy rain was also recorded over Rayalaseema, south interior Karnataka, Kerala and Mahe.
These are precisely the regions that will form the core domain of the North-East monsoon in the weeks ahead; also where the just-concluded South-West monsoon has left significant rainfall deficits.
Several rain-producing features remained in place on Tuesday evening.
Cyclonic circulations persisted over south coastal Odisha and adjoining north-west Bay of Bengal, the south-east Arabian Sea off the Kerala coast and north Tamil Nadu.
A trough stretched from the Gulf of Mannar to Madhya Maharashtra across Tamil Nadu and interior Karnataka, helping sustain the moisture feed and unstable weather over the region.

The IMD expects this broad zone of unsettled weather to persist for the next few days, with isolated heavy rain, fairly widespread to widespread rainfall, thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds likely across large parts of the South Peninsula.
This continuing activity could, in turn, prevent the withdrawal of the South-West monsoon from making substantial further progress for a few more days.
The more consequential development, however, could come from the Bay.

stories.title: Cabinet nod to new team for transport, logistics

article_sentences: The new authority would strengthen research, planning, appraisal, monitoring and impact assessment across the transportation and logistics sectors.
It would work towards harmonising planning, appraisal and monitoring of transport projects.
The ITLA will bring policy research, project planning & appraisal, monitoring & evaluation, and data analytics together under one roof.
ITLA will serve as the apex body for integrated transport and logistics planning in India.
The authority would be responsible to appraise the government infrastructure projects costing Rs 500 crore or more to ensure integrated multi-modal planning.
It will also monitor such transport and infrastructure projects, coordinate issue resolution and assess post-completion impact.
Its key role also includes the preparation of a long term transport plan covering roads, railways, ports, aviation, inland waterways, coastal shipping, urban mobility and logistics.
It would also integrate GSTN e-way bill, FASTag, Vahan, GPS and urban traffic data; use freight-flow and origin-destination analytics for evidence based project planning.
The authority would advise and assist in reviewing and updating the National Logistics Policy, 2022 and support training, skilling and capacity building across logistics sector.
It will also promote research and innovation in transport and logistics sector.

Establishment of the ITLA will play a pivotal role in realizing India’s Vision 2047 by strengthening multimodal connectivity, improving infrastructure efficiency, reducing logistics costs, and enhancing India’s global logistics competitiveness, the government said in a release.

stories.headline: CM Omar questions sudden action against Rohingyas, says ‘targeted for no reason’
stories.title: CM Omar questions sudden action against Rohingyas, says ‘targeted for no reason’
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 06: Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Tuesday questioned the “sudden” action being taken against Rohingyas, saying they were being “targeted for no reason”, while asserting that people who entered India from Bangladesh without permission could not stay in the country illegally. “People who have come from Bangladesh without permission, it is a different matter for them. But the Rohingyas, who are being targeted for no reason, when they were deported from their country, we gave them a place here. We allowed them to live here until their country’s situation improves,” Omar told reporters in Srinagar. “I find it strange to take action against them suddenly. But we do not have it in our hands. This is the Government of India,” he said. Omar added that the J&K Police is also not under the control of the Union Territory government in the matter. On the Uniform Civil Code (UCC), the Chief Minister said the J&K government would not implement it, arguing that such legislation should be debated and enacted by Parliament. “If you have the courage, bring a law in Parliament. Debate it in Parliament. See if it passes in Parliament or not,” he said. On the INDIA bloc’s campaign over alleged deletions from voter lists, Omar said the issue would continue to be raised, noting that the Supreme Court had also sought responses from the Election Commission and the Government of India over the alleged deletions. On mobile connectivity, Omar said the Cabinet had decided to allot land to BSNL in areas without mobile coverage to facilitate the installation of towers. He also said ducts were being laid along roads to avoid repeated digging by different departments for water, electricity and telecommunications works. “Where the road will be built, it would be better to use the duct so that there will be no need to dig the road again and again,” he said.—(KNO)

On the INDIA bloc’s campaign over alleged deletions from voter lists, Omar said the issue would continue to be raised, noting that the Supreme Court had also sought responses from the Election Commission and the Government of India over the alleged deletions.
On mobile connectivity, Omar said the Cabinet had decided to allot land to BSNL in areas without mobile coverage to facilitate the installation of towers.
He also said ducts were being laid along roads to avoid repeated digging by different departments for water, electricity and telecommunications works.
“Where the road will be built, it would be better to use the duct so that there will be no need to dig the road again and again,” he said.—(KNO).
